title: Orcel Agent: Core-integration planner (DeerFlow-derived MCP client), milestones M2 and M3
objective: Turn the M1 Orcel Agent (apps/orcel-agent: a standard-library MCP client of the Orcel edge with a scripted planner) into a planner that can drive a LangChain chat model, using copied and adapted DeerFlow 2.0 middlewares (loop detection, todos, compaction, tool-output budget, error and dangling-call recovery, clarification) and LangGraph checkpoints, while it stays an unprivileged client: every tool comes from the Orcel edge and every call is authorized, executed and audited by orceld. M2 and M3 of the adopted plan (docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/DEERFLOW_ORCEL_AGENT_MASTER_PLAN.md). Activation packet: docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/SG-000129.md.

include: Activate the SG-000129 contract only. Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with a fresh-context security judge.

Slice 1 (M2, dependency admission): a hash-locked Python dependency set for apps/orcel-agent only (langchain, langchain-core, langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite, mcp, langchain-mcp-adapters and their transitive closure), installed wheels-only with --require-hashes into an isolated environment; a transitive license table; an advisory audit; LangSmith and every other tracer forced off; no tiktoken; an egress-denied test; the MIT notice at apps/orcel-agent/third_party/deer-flow/LICENSE and a provenance ledger.

Slice 2 (M2, planner adapter and orchestration): a LangChain chat-model Planner adapter behind the M1 Planner protocol, and MCP tool-call orchestration whose every dispatch goes through the M1 gate (allowlist, approval budget, refusal-is-final, step budget, resume invariant). Tests use only LangChain's in-process fake chat models (labelled scripted); scripted parity with M1 on BM-02 Tier A.
Slice 3 (M2, loop detection): COPY DeerFlow's loop-detection middleware closure with Orcel tool names and port its tests.

Slice 4 (M3, context middlewares): todos and summarization (LangChain built-ins plus DeerFlow deltas), the tool-output budget and synopsis (in memory, or only in the private store), tool-error handling and dangling-call repair mapped to the resume invariant, and clarification (a question is never consent).

Slice 5 (M3, persistent planning): LangGraph SQLite checkpoints for plan and message state inside the private per-run store, under the M1 store rules plus an explicit owner-only protected DACL on Windows; kill-and-resume tests.

Slice 6 (evaluation): BM-02 Tier A and the synthetic middleware tasks (loop trap, long context, oversized output, injected instructions, kill and resume) through the agent against M1, reporting success, refusals, latency, peak memory, context growth, recovery and security failures; every row labelled deterministic-scripted.
exclude: Any change to orceld, its policy, approval broker, leases, journal, hosts or providers; any new MCP tool, argument, profile or edge behaviour.
DeerFlow sandboxes (local, AIO, E2B, OpenSandbox, Boxlite, Kubernetes), bash, file, browser and computer-control tools, and any other path that executes, reads or writes outside the Orcel edge.
DeerFlow's gateway, auth, channels, scheduler, persistence, frontend and telemetry; any listener or network client other than the stdio pipe to the edge.
Mutating or approval-bearing tools in the agent allowlist: it stays the M1 read-only set until a read-only lease-state signal exists under a separately decided change.
Model inference with real weights, model or tokenizer downloads, and hosted model providers (M4, founder decision 2).
Runtime skill installation, memory and subagents (M6), packaging, exposure, Control Room integration and release (M7).
Running the agent against an orceld that may hold a Full User or Admin lease; tests use a test orceld only.

authority_delta.activation: None. This packet authorizes implementing and proving SG-000129; it adds no dependency, donor code, tool, listener or authority.
authority_delta.orceld: None. orceld, its policy, approval broker, leases, journal, hosts and providers are unchanged; the agent is one more MCP client.
authority_delta.mcp: None. No MCP tool, argument, profile or edge behaviour changes; the agent keeps its M1 read-only allowlist.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules: every approval is asked by orceld's broker of the person; the agent never sees, mints, caches or relays an approval or lease, keeps its per-run approval budget, and stops at the first denial.
authority_delta.dependencies: Proposed only (slice 1): a hash-locked, wheels-only Python dependency set for apps/orcel-agent only, with a license table and advisory audit; nothing in orceld, the edge or any shipped artifact depends on it.
authority_delta.donor_code: Proposed only (slices 2 to 5): copied or adapted MIT-licensed DeerFlow 2.0 middleware code under apps/orcel-agent, with provenance headers, the verbatim license and a ledger; no execution, sandbox, tool or network code.
authority_delta.agent_state: Proposed only (slice 5): plan and message checkpoints inside the M1 private per-run store (owner-only, size-capped, expiring, deleted on completion).
authority_delta.network: None. No socket or listener; LangSmith and every tracer stay off and an egress-denied test enforces it.
authority_delta.process: None. The agent still spawns exactly one child, the built edge.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

decisions.question: Open the governed change
decisions.decision: Founder decision of 2026-10-30, relayed by the implementing session and recorded on issue #536: "I reaffirm my founder authorization to copy, adapt, refactor, and rebrand appropriately licensed DeerFlow 2.0 code for Orcel. You are authorized to initiate the formal SpecGrain activation process for: Orcel Agent — Core-integration planner (DeerFlow-derived MCP client). Use the adopted architecture in: docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/DEERFLOW_ORCEL_AGENT_MASTER_PLAN.md. Prepare the complete activation specification, security analysis, dependency admission, acceptance tests, and independent review. Do not treat this instruction alone as a completed SpecGrain activation. Activate the grain only after satisfying the repository's formal governance and decision requirements." The same directive limits the agent to an unprivileged MCP client with orceld as the sole execution and approval authority, keeps it unexposed and unshipped, and forbids runtime skill installation, unexpected network egress, approval bypass, Full User lease assumptions, and model inference or downloads before the model-selection and licensing gates.

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: SG-000129 runs as an additional active grain beside SG-000096, SG-000127 and SG-000128. It touches only apps/orcel-agent, tests/benchmarks and the agent's CI job, which none of them touch.

decisions.question: Rule change: the lawful open-grain set
decisions.decision: The canonical open-grain rule (apps/orcel-mcp/src/openai-plugin.test.ts and p20-architecture.test.ts) allowed SG-000096, SG-000127 and SG-000128 together. It now also allows SG-000096, SG-000127, SG-000128 and SG-000129 together, only while CURRENT.md records SG-000129's founder decision, the parallel grains SG-000108, SG-000120 and SG-000126 stay closed, and no other grain beyond SG-000096 exists. This follows the SG-000128 precedent (issue #515). No other rule changes.

decisions.question: Dependency versions
decisions.decision: Start from the versions the DeerFlow pin 81e1ab8 resolves in its backend/uv.lock (langchain 1.3.14, langchain-core 1.4.9, langgraph 1.2.9, langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2, langgraph-prebuilt 1.1.0, mcp 1.30.0, langchain-mcp-adapters 0.2.2, pydantic 2.13.3), because the copied middlewares subclass those LangChain built-ins and were tested against them. A version moves only to fix a recorded advisory or a test failure, and every move is recorded in the lock's notes. Every admitted package must be under an OSI-approved permissive license (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, PSF, ISC) or be recorded and reviewed in the license table before admission.

decisions.question: Use DeerFlow's agent factory or a thin loop
decisions.decision: A thin loop on LangChain's create_agent with the copied self-contained middlewares; DeerFlow's agents/factory.py (a 101k-line import closure with sandbox defaulting to true) is not imported.

decisions.question: Who holds the MCP session
decisions.decision: Only the M1 gate holds the edge session. LangChain tools handed to the model are thin proposals that call the gate; langchain-mcp-adapters may be used to convert the edge's tool schemas, but no adapter-created session, client or tool may call the edge directly. A source scan pins this.

decisions.question: Agent source scan scope
decisions.decision: The M1 source scan (one allowlisted spawn, no shell, no socket, no writes outside the store) keeps covering every file under apps/orcel-agent/orcel_agent, including copied donor files, and is not weakened. Third-party packages are not source-scanned; they are bounded by the hash lock, the license table, the advisory audit and the runtime egress-denied and process tests.

decisions.question: Evaluation labels
decisions.decision: Every SG-000129 benchmark row is labelled deterministic-scripted (a fake chat model replaying a plan or the tasks' scripted plans). No row is presented as autonomous model performance; that needs M4's model decision.

invariants: orceld remains the sole execution and approval authority; the agent only proposes calls over MCP stdio to the Orcel edge.
The agent spawns exactly one child process, the built edge, and opens no socket or listener.
Every dispatch passes the M1 gate: the read-only allowlist, the step budget, the per-run approval budget (default 3, stop at the first denial), refusal-is-final and the resume invariant.
A call dispatched but not recorded is surfaced as OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never re-dispatched from agent state; the planner must re-observe first.
Tool results, file and page text, summaries, todos and checkpoints are untrusted data; the system prompt is static Orcel text.
A model's finish is a claim, not a receipt; completion is judged from orceld results and task checkers.
Agent state lives only in the private per-run store: owner-only, size-capped, expiring, deleted when the run ends.
No DeerFlow sandbox, shell, file, browser, computer-control, gateway, telemetry or skill-install code is imported.
Every copied or adapted file names its DeerFlow path and the pin, and the verbatim MIT license ships beside it.
No model weights, tokenizer files or other runtime downloads; tests run with egress denied.
acceptance: Slice 1: the lock installs with pip --require-hashes --only-binary :all: on Windows, macOS and Linux with Python 3.12; the license table covers every installed distribution and admits only the recorded licenses; the advisory audit reports no unaddressed advisory; importing the agent and its dependencies with sockets denied opens no connection; LangSmith tracing is off even when the environment asks for it.

Slice 2: the LangChain adapter, driven by an in-process fake chat model, solves BM-02 Tier A through the real edge and a test orceld on all three OSes with the same calls, refusals and audit records as M1; a model proposing a tool outside the allowlist, malformed arguments or an extra approval-bearing call is refused by the gate before dispatch; the only edge session is the gate's.
Slice 3: the ported loop-detection tests pass with Orcel tool names; a loop trap stops at the hard limit and the decision is recorded.

Slice 4: ported todo, summarization, output-budget, error and dangling-call tests pass; a summary or todo containing an instruction cannot add a tool or widen an argument; an oversized result is budgeted in memory or in the private store only; a dangling call after compaction is still OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.

Slice 5: killing the agent between dispatch and recording, then resuming from the checkpoint, yields OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and a re-observation, never a re-dispatch; the checkpoint file is in the private store, owner-only (mode 0700 on Unix, a protected owner-only DACL on Windows), size-capped, expires, and is deleted on completion.

Slice 6: a report comparing M2/M3 with M1 on BM-02 Tier A and the synthetic tasks, with success, Orcel calls and refusals, approval requests, p50 and p95 step and task time, peak RSS, context size over time, loop and compaction events, resume outcomes and any security failure; every row labelled deterministic-scripted.
Every slice: the agent source scan, the egress-denied test and the M1 tests still pass; the agent is not packaged and not referenced by orceld.
Exact-head CI (Windows, macOS and Linux legs), Review Gates where they run, and a fresh-context security judge pass on each slice; d1-local is advisory only.

review.alibaba_open_code_review: delegation mode per standing founder decision (2026-10-10) with manual review of excluded files, where functional
review.security_review: fresh-context security judge on the activation, every slice and closeout, with an explicit supply-chain review on slice 1; d1-local advisory only

successor_requirements.m4: Local-model evaluation needs founder decision 2 (model, license, how users obtain it).
successor_requirements.mutating_tools: A mutating allowlist needs a read-only lease-state signal, a separately decided edge change.
successor_requirements.m6_m7: Subagents, memory and skills (M6), packaging and Control Room integration (M7) are outside SG-000129.

activation_note: No dependency, donor code, tool or authority change in this activation packet. Separate implementation PRs must qualify their exact heads; activation CI alone proves nothing about the agent.
done_when: The Orcel Agent runs BM-02 Tier A and the synthetic middleware tasks through a LangChain planner adapter with the copied DeerFlow middlewares and SQLite checkpoints on Windows, macOS and Linux CI, with every call authorized and audited by orceld, the resume invariant held across a kill, no egress, a hash-locked license-reviewed dependency set, and a labelled comparison with M1.
